title: Praying in the Name of Christ
speaker: Elder Nick Anderson

outline.title: Prayer is Required
subpoints: Prayer is an act of obedience to God's command.
The first instance of prayer is found in Genesis 4:26.
Prayer is the life of the soul and essential for worship.

outline.title: Pray with Confidence in God's Promises
subpoints: Human sinfulness often hinders confidence in approaching God.
Focus on Christ's mercy rather than personal merit.
Avoid excessive introspection that leads to despair.

outline.title: Praying in the Name of Christ is Not Merely Verbal
subpoints: It is not a magic formula or mere formality.
It involves drawing encouragement and boldness from Christ's mediation.
True prayer is grounded in the person and work of Christ.

summary:
This lesson continues the Sunday school series on the Westminster Larger Catechism, focusing on Questions 180 and 181 regarding the nature of praying in the name of Christ. The teaching emphasizes that prayer is not optional but a commanded duty, rooted in the earliest biblical records and exemplified by Christ and the apostles. It is described as the life of the soul, essential for true worship and spiritual vitality.

The sermon addresses the common struggle of approaching a holy God with confidence. It encourages believers to look less at their own sinfulness and more at the mercy of Christ, warning against the despair that can result from excessive self-examination. By focusing on God's character and promises, believers can approach the throne of grace with boldness.

Finally, the lesson clarifies that praying in the name of Christ is not a magical incantation or a mere verbal formula. Instead, it signifies a deep reliance on Christ's mediation, drawing strength, hope, and acceptance from His work rather than personal merit. This understanding transforms prayer from a ritual into a confident communion with God.
